points: Q2 already delivered $3.27B in net sales (+24%) and adjusted EPS of $1.52 (+60%), so the Q3 print will test whether the second-half ramp can carry the raised $14B full-year sales guidance.
The print will reveal if adjusted operating margin can hold near the Q2 22.6% level, which is the leverage needed for the FY1 consensus of $6.71 EPS to land inside the $6.65-$6.75 guided range.

Q3 order commentary and backlog conversion will show whether large AI data center deployments are moving past the 'lengthy and unpredictable procurement' risk flagged in Q2 filings, setting Q4 revenue visibility.

With adjusted free cash flow at $925M in Q2 and capex guided to roughly 4% of sales, the print will show if cash generation remains strong enough to fund capacity expansion without pressuring margins.

The FY2 consensus of $9.10 EPS (+35.6%) depends on continued operating leverage; Q3 guidance and margin trajectory will indicate whether that growth is achievable and whether the theme-relative discount valuation flag is supported.

With 21 estimate raises versus 3 cuts in the last 30 days and a +3.44% revenue estimate move, the Q3 print needs to validate continued estimate momentum; peer prints from INTC (Oct 23) and AMD (Nov 4) may add data-center demand context but VRT's own bookings and guidance are decisive.
watch: Q3 organic sales growth at or above the ~31% full-year guidance run-rate — supports the long.
Adjusted operating margin holding above 22% — supports the long.
FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance maintained or raised toward the $6.70 midpoint/consensus — supports the long.
Q3 adjusted free cash flow remaining robust versus the ~4% capex plan — supports the long.
